title: JANUS Tear falsification campaign
definition: A JANUS Tear is a compact independently checkable invariant condensed from one or more residual SAT states.

canonical_context.boundary: C020 does not refute H127; it attacks broader all-state and concrete policy Tear formulations.

positive_result.tear: one component-charge parity bit per component

falsified_candidates.name: bounded-local complete Tear language
falsified_candidates.reason: C017 and H125 provide opposite-label twins with equal bounded-radius signed-incidence views.

falsified_candidates.name: unsigned structure plus signed marginals
falsified_candidates.reason: An exact three-variable SAT/UNSAT pair shares all implemented marginal features.

falsified_candidates.name: unit-propagation-enhanced structural marginals
falsified_candidates.reason: A ternary SAT/UNSAT pair has an identical exhaustive unit-propagation profile.

falsified_candidates.name: fixed bounded-width resolution Tears
falsified_candidates.reason: The odd-charge K4 Tseitin contradiction has no width-three refutation but has a width-four refutation.

falsified_candidates.name: visible affine/XOR extraction
falsified_candidates.reason: The bijection x=b XOR (a AND c) preserves semantics while hiding the relation from an affine-only extractor.

falsified_candidates.name: polynomial continuation-complete quotient of all residual states
falsified_candidates.reason: E_n(X,Y)=AND_i(x_i<->y_i) has O(n) size but produces 2^n pairwise continuation-distinguishable residuals after assigning X.

falsified_candidates.name: Policy-0A under the explicit state envelope B(v)=4v^2
policy: at most 4 times the residual literal count resolution-pair attempts
at most max(8, clause_count/4) added resolvents
derived width at most current maximum plus one
most-frequent-variable branching with smallest-index tie break
falsified_candidates.boundary: Finite falsification of one exact policy and one quadratic state promise; not an asymptotic lower bound.

tear_trilemma.decision_only: Only two classes are needed, but extracting the class is SAT and is circular.
tear_trilemma.continuation_complete: The equality family forces exponentially many classes.
tear_trilemma.policy_selected: An explicit polynomial policy that always succeeds is already a polynomial-time SAT algorithm.

surviving_candidate.name: JANUS Tear Guided-Policy Candidate
surviving_candidate.statement: One explicit polynomial-time Tear language and transition policy generates only polynomially many polynomially verifiable Tears and states on every CNF and returns a SAT witness or sound rejection artifact.
surviving_candidate.consequence_if_true: SAT is in P and therefore P=NP.

next_gate: Select an explicit bounded-degree expander family and prove or refute a superpolynomial lower bound for the fully specified masked policy on residual states, proof work, normalization work, or witness-recovery information.
claim_boundary: The strong universal quotient and several restricted policies are refuted. No result proves P=NP, proves P!=NP, or validates an unspecified policy by failure to find a counterexample.
